newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures rallied early on Tuesday, tagging Bunds, to set a contract high but failed to hold onto their gains as caution prevailed with a weak franc ahead of a raft of U.S. data and fresh franc bond supply.
The December contract struggled to break through last week's high of 127.54 after the positive start. It eventually broke through, hit 127.62, then drifted lower as new buyers failed to emerge.
Most traders expected the contract to remain well supported on Wednesday morning although some said the risk was that U.S. inflation numbers would unsettle bonds rather than reassure.
"The market should remain calm and well-supported ahead of the (U.S.) PPI," a trader at a French bank said. "But it's not surprising we didn't go past the highs with a weak dollar."

Traders said selling by a large French bank had been the catalyst for the late decline in the futures price. The bank sold a relatively large amount of contracts in an otherwise calm session between 127.42-46, they said.
"You don't go short in that size in this kind of market unless you've got a good reason," a futures trader at another French bank said.
The late selloff left the 10-year spread between benchmark OATs and Bunds at parity compared with minus two late on Friday. Two- and five-year French bonds also underperformed on Tuesday.

Analysts said the auction by French welfare debt repayment fund CADES should be reasonably well received although some traders speculated that the late weakness may have been due in part to covering ahead of the auction.
The fund's three French franc bonds, the 2002, 2005 and 2007 bonds, will be on offer and the fund said last week it planned to sell a total of eight to 10 billion francs.

Ciaran O'Hagan, bond analyst at JP Morgan in Paris, said although the 2005 bond looked the cheapest, the 2007 had attracted good institutional demand in the past and the 2002 bond would benefit from having the lower duration.
The results of the auction will be released from 1000 GMT on Wednesday morning.
The Treasury announced on Tuesday it would sell 300 to 500 million Ecu of 2004 and 2006 OATs on Thursday, adding to the overall supply pressures this week.

The franc was buffeted by dollar volatility. The French unit slipped to a low of 3.3868 early on Tuesday, compared with 3.3840 late on Monday but climbed to 3.3814 per mark as the dollar reached 1.50 against the German currency.
December PIBOR missed out on the late franc rise and settled down two basis points at 96.42, underperforming December Euromarks. The spread widened to 38 basis points.

Given the relative franc weakness and the fact call money hasn't budged since the last intervention rate cut on October 31, few economists expected any action after the Bank of France's monetary policy council meeting on Thursday.
